content.p: On 8 September 2025 workers at a tow yard in Hollywood called police about a strong smell coming from a Tesla that had been left in the Hollywood Hills. Inside the front trunk, investigators found the remains of a girl. She was identified as Celeste Rivas Hernandez, a 14-year-old from Lake Elsinore, California, who had first been reported missing as a seventh grader in early 2024. The car was registered to David Anthony Burke, a young singer who performs as d4vd and who was then on a world tour.

Burke was arrested in April 2026 and charged with three offences: murder in the first degree with special circumstances, repeated sexual abuse of a child younger than 14, and unlawfully mutilating a body. He has pleaded not guilty. In July 2026 a judge ruled that prosecutors had presented enough evidence for a trial. Everything below about how Celeste died comes from prosecutors, from detectives and experts who testified, or from the judge's ruling. None of it has been tested before a jury.

Celeste lived with her family in Lake Elsinore, a community in western Riverside County about 70 miles southeast of Los Angeles. In a statement released in April 2026, her family described her as a girl who loved to sing and dance and said that every Friday was movie night at home. Her brother told NBC Los Angeles in 2025 that the family knew she was acquainted with the singer.

According to a document setting out the prosecution's evidence, which CNN reviewed, Burke first met Celeste in 2022, when she was 11. Prosecutors say the relationship became sexual in November 2023, when he was 18 and she was 13. The charging papers allege that the continuous sexual abuse began on or about September 2023, the month Celeste turned 13. Reports differ slightly on the early contact: a news summary of the hearing said prosecutors alleged Burke began communicating with her when she was 12.

The family has said it knew of the acquaintance. In testimony at the preliminary hearing, a detective answering defence questions said that both sets of parents knew of the relationship, that Burke had gone to church alongside relatives of hers, and that her parents consented to a week-long trip to London with him. Celeste's family lawyer, Patrick Steinfeld, said the family was "horrified that the defense attorneys brought up evidence to put the blame on a 14-year-old girl", in the words ABC7 reported.

Celeste was reported missing three times in the first months of 2024, according to a CNN investigation. The first report came in mid-February, and a missing-person poster said she was last seen on or about 14 February. The second was around 19 March. The third, made on 5 April, was reported by the Riverside County Sheriff's Office as the final report; a missing-person flyer said she was last seen leaving home at 9 p.m. that day.

CNN reported that around the time of the first report, someone worried about her wrote to an email address in d4vd's name at his label's domain. It said there had been talk that he possibly had something to do with her disappearance and asked him to take her home because her parents were worried. CNN said it confirmed the email with its sender, who asked not to be named. An acquaintance of the family told CNN that Celeste came home within days of that message.

CNN also reported that she kept turning up near the singer. In January 2024 she appeared beside him in a Twitch livestream. A teenager posted photographs on TikTok that showed him getting out of a black Tesla a few blocks from her home. In June 2024 she was photographed backstage at a sold-out d4vd show at the Fonda Theatre in Los Angeles. A private investigator hired by the owner of the house Burke later rented said he found a digital camera there with pictures of Celeste and Burke from late December 2024 and early January 2025, which suggests she was alive then.

Prosecutors presented a minute-by-minute account of that night at the preliminary hearing, drawing on text messages recovered through search warrants on Burke's phone and iCloud accounts. They said the two argued the day before over his friendship with another woman. On 22 April Celeste sent angry messages, including "I swear to GOD I will kill u" and "I will end ur career." ABC7 quoted a related message as "i will end ur career and ur life." Prosecutors said these texts show only a minor being manipulated by an adult. Deputy District Attorney Silverman told the court: "We have a minor who was sexually abused. ... She was taught to believe that she was being gaslit."

The next afternoon, prosecutors said, the two arranged for Burke to send an Uber to bring her to his house. The prosecution says he lured her there intending to kill her. The defence says the texts show she asked for the meeting herself after becoming upset, and, as ABC7 reported, established that she had asked seven times to see him in the preceding days and that he agreed reluctantly.

At 10:02 p.m. Celeste wrote, "Girly pop, im almost there open ur door if ur home," according to CNN's account of the texts. Prosecutors said the gate was opened and the door unlocked at 10:10. It was the last text sent from her phone. LAPD Detective Corey Farrell testified that investigators think she was killed in the window from 10:10 to 10:31 p.m., when Burke resumed texting her to ask where she was. Prosecutors characterise those messages as an attempt to build a defence. Prosecutors allege he stabbed her shortly after she entered. An LAPD cellular analyst testified that Burke's phone and car left the property at about 11:30 p.m. Burke's album, "Withered", came out two days later according to ABC7, and CNN said he held a release party the day after the killing.

Prosecutors allege that Burke dismembered Celeste's body in his garage and drove around with the remains for weeks or months. The Tesla was eventually parked in the Hollywood Hills, where neighbours said it had been for more than a month, and was towed after someone reported it abandoned. When tow-yard staff noticed the smell, officers opened the front trunk and found remains in two bags, according to grand jury papers that became public after a Texas court hearing. They were found a day after what would have been her 15th birthday, and nearly five months after prosecutors say she died.

The LAPD's chief, Jim McDonnell, said the condition of the remains delayed the medical examiner's work and that the time between the death and the discovery meant crucial evidence had degraded or disappeared. No cause of death has been made public. ABC7 reported that the defence, at the hearing, cited a medical examiner's ruling of homicide from two puncture wounds and argued that this was too vague to prove murder. The defence did not offer an alternative account of how she died, and is not required to.

The forensic evidence also drew challenge. Investigators found 11 air fresheners in the Tesla, and a criminalist testified that DNA from possible blood on items in the house, including the garage floor, a Tesla charger and a rowing machine, showed a high probability of being Celeste's. Defence attorney Blair Berk replied that DNA can persist for years and can move between surfaces by secondary transfer. Two chainsaws found at the house were tested and showed no sign of blood; a third that records show Burke bought was never recovered. Prosecutors also pointed to records of purchases of chainsaws and wading pools. In January 2026 a state transportation worker found Celeste's passport card at the roadside in the hills above Santa Barbara, over 85 miles from where Burke was living. An LAPD cellular analyst testified that phone and Tesla records helped show three trips Burke allegedly took to that county.

When the singer's name began to be linked to the car, he cancelled the last US dates of his tour and the entire European leg. A spokesperson said in September that he was cooperating with authorities, but NBC Los Angeles reported in November that a police source said he no longer was.

Subpoenas issued on 15 January 2026 called for testimony from Burke's mother, father and brother before a Los Angeles County grand jury and described Burke as a "target" of the inquiry. The documents became public after his relatives appealed the subpoenas in Texas. LAPD Robbery-Homicide detectives arrested him on a Thursday in April 2026 at a home in the Hollywood Hills about a mile from the tow yard, and he was held without bail.

On 20 April District Attorney Hochman announced the charges. The special circumstances were lying in wait, murder for financial gain and murder of a witness, along with an allegation that Burke personally used a sharp instrument. Hochman said the financial-gain allegation rests on the singer's career, which prosecutors say Celeste threatened. A not guilty plea was entered the same day. His lawyers said "the actual evidence in this case will show that David Burke did not murder Celeste Rivas Hernandez and he was not the cause of her death". His family said it stood by him "one hundred percent".

The five-day hearing began on 20 July 2026. More than ten witnesses testified. A deputy medical examiner said the dismembered body parts were potentially consistent with a chainsaw or other power tool, that the exact tool could not be determined, and that it was impossible to say whether it was used before or after death. A detective described explicit photographs and messages found on Burke's phone; the prosecutor said the images were not shown in court because they are considered child sexual abuse material. Text messages also referred to a pregnancy and an abortion, including a message from Burke that read "let this abortion be the last one till we have the real one", according to ABC7. Financial witnesses said his music earned him at least $10 million between 2023 and 2025.

Celeste's parents attended most of the hearing, leaving the room during the autopsy testimony and the description of the photographs. On 27 July Judge Olmedo ruled that prosecutors had shown probable cause on all counts and special circumstances, ordered Burke held without bail and set an arraignment for 31 August. Hochman said the hearing showed only a small fraction of the evidence. The defence argued that the murder evidence was insufficient; ABC7 reported that it did not argue against the other two charges. Billboard noted that a preliminary hearing uses a lower standard than a trial, which needs proof beyond a reasonable doubt.

On 31 August Burke's private lawyers, Blair Berk and Marilynne Bednarski and their team, were allowed to withdraw without giving a reason, and public defender Walid Kandeel took over. Kandeel asked for the arraignment to be postponed, but the judge refused, and Burke again pleaded not guilty. Celeste's family objected in a statement that Burke is not poor and accused him of hiding money in corporations; that is the family's claim, and the report did not confirm it. Hochman said the decision on seeking the death penalty has not been made and that the defence had not returned a mitigation packet before the earlier lawyers withdrew. Former prosecutor Joshua Ritter told ABC7 New York that premeditation could be the hardest point for prosecutors, and that the defence could argue that without eyewitnesses or confessions the evidence is circumstantial.
The judge set a status conference for 19 October 2026. Hochman said the trial should start within 90 days of that date unless the defence asks for more time.
